chunk-001:c001.proposition: The best explanation of all contingent things cannot be another contingent member of that totality and therefore points to an automatically actual, noncontingent foundation.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move independently states the opening inference from the contingent totality, through avoidance of explanatory circularity, to a noncontingent foundation.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Necessity admits different strengths, allowing the argument to reject maximal epistemic certainty while retaining a weaker foundational status such as inability to begin or cease.

orphanFallback.rationale: Even without the preceding conceivability objection, distinguishing strengths of necessity positively specifies a modest modal conclusion for the proposed foundation.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Careful inquiry may extend ordinary and scientific inference-to-the-best-explanation practices to reality as a whole, thereby favoring an explanatory foundation over brute contingency.

orphanFallback.rationale: The analogy with ordinary and scientific inquiry independently supplies a positive method for investigating ultimate reality while preserving epistemic humility.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Actuality that could have failed specially calls for explanation, whereas an automatically actual foundation avoids that demand and may derive its necessity from its supreme nature.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move independently identifies contingency as the feature generating the explanatory demand and presents automatic actuality as the relevant stopping condition.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: For any contingent things there is an explanation of their existence, and the explanation of all contingent things cannot itself be among the contingent things being explained.

orphanFallback.rationale: The formulation stands independently as the argument's operative explanatory principle and its anti-circular application to the complete contingent collection.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Brute contingency is explanatorily worse than brute necessity because an automatically actual foundation does not invite a deeper explanation in the way a contingent fact does.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a comparative abductive claim, the proposition independently gives a reason to prefer an automatically actual endpoint over an unexplained contingent endpoint.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Objective necessary principles of logic may belong to reality's foundational layer, with human reasoning tracking rules that remain true independently of human minds.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move positively locates mind-independent logical structure within foundational reality and so supplies content for an automatically actual foundation.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Conceivability of a godless world does not establish genuine possibility because contradictions can emerge only through extended inference, while the contingency argument may independently indicate such a contradiction.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of a retained objection, the move supplies a general modal distinction between apparent conceivability and possibility and assigns evidential work to the contingency argument.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Calling a foundation brute means only that it has no further explanation; a necessary nature can still distinguish that foundation from ordinary contingent and dependent things.

orphanFallback.rationale: The distinction independently clarifies that explanatory fundamentality and contingency are not equivalent, leaving a necessary unexplained foundation conceptually coherent.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: If a merely contingent foundation would remain open to a better further explanation, inquiry into reality's structure gives reason to assign its foundation a more robust nature than ordinary contingent objects possess.

orphanFallback.rationale: The move independently develops an abductive route from the availability of a better explanation to a more robust, nonordinary character for the foundation.
